D5: bearer-token and sendgrid-token twin/differential findings — fixture encodes a superseded or conflated expectation, no detector defect

disposition.reason: All five findings reduce to two already-shipped, evidence-reviewed detector decisions, not a detector defect. The three bearer-token-header twins mutate a byte that still leaves both sides of a 40-byte value at or above MIN_TOKEN_LEN (16), so no single mid-value mutation at this index can produce a negative under the documented floor; the twin's chosen mutation index is untenable given that already-tested contract. The sendgrid base62-bearer-twin is correctly declined by sendgrid-token's own exact-length contract but is separately, correctly co-detected by bearer-token as a generic Bearer credential (67 bytes, well over the 16-byte floor) -- expected co-detection, not a discrimination failure. base62-generic-key-twin is a mainline generic-token true positive under the standing decision https://github.com/redact-secret/redact-secret/blob/de6add470321f40d7b1cb36808d9f4559e6c2e99/docs/decisions/2026-09-20-warn-unconditionally-on-high-signal-contextual-names.md (api_key= is a HIGH_SIGNAL_NAMES match, warned on unconditionally). Correcting the three benchmark fixtures (moving the bearer-token-header twin's mutation within 16 bytes of either edge; rescoping the two sendgrid twins to expect co-detection) is redact-secret-benchmarks follow-up work, not filed as of this record.

disposition.reason: Maintainer decision 2026-09-24: generic-token flagging the public Confluent API key ID in the JSON "apiKey" field is accepted behaviour, not a defect. A 16-character random value under an apiKey name cannot be distinguished from a real API key (e.g. an Alpha Vantage key) without cross-line context, and the key ID is the paired companion of the secret, so redacting it leaks nothing. The finding had been promoted to redact-secret#739 on 2026-09-24; that issue is closed as not planned and no benchmark-gap-739 product manifest record is expected. Benchmark side (#213): the key-ID span [15,31) in beta8-209--confluent-cloud-api-secret-secrets-manager-json and in its alphabet twin is authored with the corpus schema's companion span role (docs/specs/measurement-v4.md), so redacting it is never required and costs no collateral; the family's standalone public-ID controls stay must-not-flag. The observation evidence below is kept at the corpus hash it was measured against.

Policy: submitted-range misses outside the raw-input contract (RFC display-wrapped JWT and JWK figures; a percent-encoded URL with no access_token parameter under standard parsing)

disposition.reason: Maintainer decision (redact-secret#822, adjudicated per fixture in #322): no beta.9 line joining or percent decoding. The three first-run misses are historical misses of the submitted ranges, not confirmed product false negatives under the raw-input contract. rfc7519-jwt-display-breaks and rfc7515-jwk-k-display-break are presentation-only examples: RFC 7519 section 3.1 and RFC 7515 appendix A.1.1 insert those line breaks for display only, so the bytes are not a compact JWT and not valid JSON, and the jwt and same-line JWK grammars do not join display-wrapped lines. This is detector-specific: the PEM private-key detector spans lines by design. composed-percent-encoded-url-in-json is a downstream-normalization scenario: its = and & are percent-encoded, and the WHATWG urlencoded parser splits on literal delimiters before decoding, so the URL has no access_token parameter (its one parameter is named access_token=<token>&p=q, with an empty value). Only an application that decodes the whole URL before parsing produces that parameter; that transform needs its own scenario and does not make the bytes safe for every consumer. The pack's expectations and first run are unchanged; the per-fixture adjudication is adversarial/packs/beta9-external-inputs/adjudication.json, which also keeps the superseded wording.

issues.title: Policy: keyword-scanner shapes outside the contextual-assignment contract (reversed comparison, C++ constructor argument, `db_pass`)

disposition.reason: Maintainer decision: the db_pass fixture (ds-keyword-non-ascii-secret) is fixed by redact-secret#838 (merge 54e55fefe34255ecf77a4f635792d8d566eefeb1), which makes db_pass a high-signal name as the exact whole name; on that commit the fixture reports the expected 10-23 range at warn/medium because the value is under 16 bytes (the #825 policy). The reversed comparison (ds-keyword-reversed-comparison) and the C++ constructor argument (ds-cpp-string-constructor) stay unfixed as policy: comparison grammar would flag test assertions, and call arguments would match accessor calls whose argument is a name. The record is annotated rather than split because a second record for #823 would need a product manifest record id that no promotion created.

issues.title: Policy: warn on short literals under high-signal names in benign code (`"somefakekey"`, `"#add-password"`)

disposition.reason: Maintainer decision (keep current policy): already decided by the accepted record that warns unconditionally on high-signal contextual names. A short literal under a high-signal name warns without redacting because it could be a real weak password; splitting placeholder words out of larger runs or excluding #kebab-case values would drop real passwords. The first-run schema records ranges only and so counts a warn as a flag.

issues.title: Policy: short values under high-signal names warn instead of redact (beta9 adversarial pack)

disposition.reason: Maintainer decision (keep current policy): a value under 16 bytes under a high-signal name is medium confidence by design, and contextual_secret is confidence-gated, so it warns instead of redacting. Real OAuth access tokens are longer than the 15-byte RFC 6750 example. Revisit only through the confidence-scoring work (redact-secret#767/#771).

Policy: a Cohere key under a masked_-led name (LiteLLM proxy debug log) is not reported

disposition.reason: Documented policy, not a defect: the value sits under a masked_-led key, and decision-redact-provider-named-credential-assignments section 2 says a prefix whose first segment says the value is not the secret (redacted_, masked_, hashed_, ...) does not make a high-signal name, so generic-token does not report it and the Cohere detector has no keyword on the line. The #932 fix (127260c) left it unreported by design, and product manifest record benchmark-gap-932 records it as a policy note. Split out of product-932 so that record is verified on the three forms the fix covers; the fixture expectation is unchanged. Candidate 1db8ff3 (run 009a85fa-e810-4ab8-85a5-a264dba30536) still misses it. A changed policy is a new observation, not an edit of this record. Reopened as a proposal on 2026-09-29 by redact-secret#1018 (security-first: report a complete, unmasked key under a masked_-led name, keep genuinely masked values silent); a fix is in progress on the product branch beta12/provisional-fixes. Until a release changes the policy this record stands; when it does, the fixture moves to a new product-1018 record.

disposition.reason: Documented confidence-gated policy, not a defect: each span is detected exactly at medium confidence because the provider keyword is elsewhere on the line (or on an earlier line) and the value is not assigned to a provider-named or high-signal key, and policy.rs warns at medium for these confidence-gated types (decision-redact-provider-named-credential-assignments section 1). None of the eight is under a provider-named key. redact-secret#936 asks the maintainers to confirm the one open point (the twilio row sits under auth_token, which generic-token treats as ambiguous while a text.rs doc comment names it as high-signal); a changed answer is a new observation, not an edit of this record.
